nonblocking_findings: Essa is complete in both languages. HE and EN each have 44 stanza milestones in the same order with matching URNs, one-to-one. No ordinal stanza_N URNs are emitted. Every stanza is closed by a bare stanza terminator. The ק׳/קהל and חזן rubric notes sit outside stanza scope. There are no empty or unfilled translations.

The other 42 stanza slugs check out against the transliteration rules: dagesh doubling, sounded/silent shva, tsere+yod → ei, no apostrophes. Human reading יֹקֶשׁ (holam) is present at HE line 120, and the slug 'yoqesh' matches it.

Page breaks are consistent. HE pages 137–143 map to n293, n295, …, n305 and EN pages to n294, …, n306, which fits the facs n = PDF scan − 1 convention for facing pages. All pb@n values increase monotonically and match between languages.

The HE essa file has no explicit opening pb for page 137, only div@facs n293. The EN file opens with pb n=137 at n294. This is probably due to earlier content on HE page 137 in a preceding file, but I could not confirm that within this scope.

The shofarot chain has exactly 17 verse units in both languages, in the same order as the bible projection proof. Ex 20:18 uses canonical n=18 and source bible:exodus/20/18, not the traditional 15. The HE Ex 20:18 seg crosses pb 143 (n305), so it carries both leaves. Second Ex 19 occurrence uses its own context URN (occurrence_19), so nothing is duplicated.

Every chapter and verse scope closes with matching bare terminators before the next intro prayer-part. Zech 9:15 is a named verse-part (adonai_tzevaot_yagen) under a partial_15 chapter context. It is closed by verse-part, then verse, then chapter terminators, and makes no claim to the whole chapter or verse.

Ken tagen appears once as a prayer-part in each language's ken_tagen_words stream (HE n305, EN n306, page 143), closed by a bare terminator. ken_tagen_weekday transcludes it once per language with matching @ids. Slug ken_tagen_al_ammekha_yisrael is correctly transliterated.
The EN Psalm 150:6 sic/corr adds the closing quotation mark. It is an editorial choice that is visible in the file; it is not drift.
scope_limitations: I did not compare against the source images. Exactness of words, pointing and punctuation rests on the supplied proofs: rendered-stanza-projection-proof-v3 (essa he/en, 44 stanzas, exact) and bible-source-projection-proof (shofarot_verses he/en, exact). Accepted readings were not reopened.
The supplied evidence has no separate 180-row compiled-proof file. The two proof files listed above are the evidence I relied on.
I could not check whether the EN essa omits Cong./Reader rubrics because the English printing lacks them.
Where ken tagen sits in the shared spine ('expanded once after alternatives') is covered by the separate shared-spine review. Here I only checked that each stream transcludes it exactly once.
Header metadata, code, export and the other groups are out of scope.
verdict: Not approved. Two stanza URN slugs, essa_dei_betzedeq/hakhshal and /haonash, break the qamatz-qatan transliteration rule and should be renamed to /hokhshal and /hoonash in HE, EN and the incipit decisions record. Everything else in scope passes: 44-stanza HE/EN coverage and boundaries, the 17-verse shofarot chain with canonical Ex 20:18 and its cross-page scope, the bounded Zech 9:15 verse-part, the ken tagen home and single transclusion, page-boundary facs, and complete translations with no drift. Re-review only needs to confirm the two renamed URNs.
